method: Questions were researched with an evidence-only retrieval tool over one corpus of open-access and public-domain texts (see corpus.json). Each excerpt was checked word for word against the corpus passage it cites when this file was written; corpus_chunk numbers that passage in the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-01.
questions: What different kinds of definition are there, and what goals do they serve?
What is the difference between real and nominal definitions?
What is an explication, and how does it differ from stipulative and descriptive definitions?
What can stipulative and ostensive definitions do that others cannot?

evidence.excerpt: we speak of a commission as defining the boundary between two nations; of the Supreme Court as defining, through its rulings, “person” and “citizen”; of a chemist as discovering the definition of gold, and the lexicographer, that of ‘cool’
the boundary commission may aim to achieve precision; the Supreme Court, fairness; the chemist and the lexicographer, accuracy; the debater, clarity; and the mathematician, fecundity
John Locke distinguished, in his Essay, “real essence” from “nominal essence.”
The chemist aims at real definition, whereas the lexicographer aims at nominal definition.

Whether the search for an answer to the Socratic question “What is virtue?” is a search for real definition or one for nominal definition depends upon one’s conception of this particular philosophical activity.
A stipulative definition imparts a meaning to the defined term, and involves no commitment that the assigned meaning agrees with prior uses (if any) of the term.
Descriptive definitions, like stipulative ones, spell out meaning, but they also aim to be adequate to existing usage.
a lack of fit with existing usage is an objection to them
An explication aims to respect some central uses of a term but is stipulative on others.
But the mismatch is not an objection to the explication. What is important for explication is not antecedent meaning but function.
the truth-functional conditional can be put forward as an explication of the ordinary conditional for certain purposes in certain contexts
to uphold the definition of “ordered pair” as a philosophical paradigm
Here, the pair \(\langle x,y\rangle\) is defined as the set \(\{\{x\}, \{x,y\}\}\).
When an epistemologist seeks a definition of “knowledge,” she is not seeking a good dictionary entry for the word ‘know’.
If one stipulatively defines a “raimex” as, say, a rational, imaginative, experiencing being then the judgment “raimexes are rational” is assured of being necessary, certain, and a priori.
Philosophers have found it tempting to explain the puzzling cases of, e.g., a priori judgments, by an appeal to stipulative definitions.
the description serves only to fix the reference of the new name; the name is not synonymous with the description
Unlike other familiar definitions, ostensive definitions can introduce terms that are ineliminable.
all nominal definitions, if pushed back far enough, must lead ultimately to terms having only ostensive definitions
Dictionaries aim to provide definitions that contain sufficient information to impart an understanding of the term.
